name: R Lakshmanan
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Shanthi Feeds (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu)
profile: Founded Shanthi Feeds in 1988 as a small poultry farm in Pappampatti, near Coimbatore; it grew into an integrated broiler business (hatcheries, poultry and cattle feed mills, processing, soya/corn cultivation) with capacity of ~47 million birds a year, and also runs wind energy projects.
interesting_fact: Shanthi Feeds has set up more than 1,000 contract broiler farms over 30 years and in 2019 commissioned a Petersime single-stage hatchery able to hatch 14+ million eggs a year; the group also invests in wind energy.
deep_cut_fact: He started the business in Pappampatti, a rain-shadow area so dry that conventional farming was limited, and expanded with the explicit aim of creating paid work in the village.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Alive status not confirmed though a 'Lakshmanan, Shanthi Hatcheries' chaired a Poultry Farmers Regulatory Committee summit in Nov 2025 (businessminutes.in). Wind-energy angle may suit the energy podcast. Best route: company website/office in Coimbatore.

name: Bian Xingcai
profile: Former actual controller of Sanfangxiang Group (Jiangyin, Jiangsu; polyester/PET, textiles, chemicals), listed vehicle Sanfangxiang 600370.SH. Died 6 March 2024; his stake passed by inheritance to his children (Bian Pinggang, Bian Huigang, Bian Pingfang).
notes: Deceased 6 March 2024 per Sanfangxiang (600370) takeover report filed Nov 2024: https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202411181640939154_1.pdf . Rest skipped per instructions. Group now controlled by the next generation.

name: Vamanrai V Parekh
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Nilkamal Ltd (stepped down from the board in Aug 2020)
profile: First-generation entrepreneur who, with brother Sharad, left the family button business in 1981 to make plastic household goods in a rented shed in Powai, Mumbai. That became Nilkamal, the listed maker of moulded plastic furniture, material-handling crates/pallets, mattresses and @Home retail. He was Chairman 1990-2020 and is now Chairman Emeritus; sons Hiten and Manish are in the business.
interesting_fact: Nilkamal describes itself as the world's largest producer of moulded plastic furniture, selling in about 30 countries; it has been listed on NSE/BSE since 1991.
deep_cut_fact: The crate business that made Nilkamal began when the brothers noticed wooden crates carrying milk bottles at Worli Dairy and realised plastic crates would be lighter, more durable and cheaper. The family firm itself traces back to a one-machine metal-button shed their father Vrajlal Parekh started in 1934.
notes: Elderly (about 88 per data providers) and retired from the board in 2020; no recent public statements found, and no death reports found. Hurun wealth shared with brother Sharad V Parekh. Best route: via Nilkamal company secretary or investor relations. The 1934 button-shed detail comes from Nilkamal's 'Our Journey' page (https://nilkamal.com/?p=201).

name: Dominic Frederico
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Assured Guaranty Ltd (NYSE: AGO)
profile: Has led bond insurer Assured Guaranty since December 2003, taking it public in 2004 and building it into the leading municipal bond insurer and financial guarantor, notably by buying FSA in 2009 (renamed Assured Guaranty Municipal). Before that he was President/COO of ACE Limited and spent about 13 years at AIG. More recently he pushed into alternative asset management and, in Jan 2026, annuity reinsurance (Assured Life Re).
interesting_fact: In January 2026 Assured Guaranty entered annuity reinsurance by acquiring a life and annuity reinsurer it renamed Assured Life Re; by mid-2026 he reported record per-share book value metrics.
deep_cut_fact: At ACE (1995-2003) he was the deal executive behind ACE's purchase of CIGNA's property-casualty business and the Capital Re acquisition. That Capital Re platform later became the core of Assured Guaranty, the company he has run since 2003.
notes: Media contact is Ashweeta Durani (Director, Media Relations, 212-408-6042) and IR contact is Robert Tucker; both are listed in the Q2 2026 earnings release. Little personal or public-profile information exists beyond earnings calls. Assured Guaranty insures infrastructure bonds such as JFK New Terminal One, which could be a relevant hook for energy and infrastructure topics.

name: Donald G Macpherson
current_role: Chairman & CEO, W.W. Grainger (NYSE: GWW); Director, DuPont de Nemours
profile: D.G. Macpherson has been CEO of industrial MRO distributor Grainger since October 2016 and Chairman since October 2017. He joined Grainger in 2008 from Boston Consulting Group, where he was a partner and managing director, and previously ran global supply chain and international operations before serving as COO. He has led Grainger's push into high-touch and endless-assortment (Zoro, MonotaRO) e-commerce models and, more recently, AI.
interesting_fact: Under his tenure Grainger has split into two models: 'High-Touch Solutions' for large customers, and an 'Endless Assortment' online business (Zoro in the US, MonotaRO in Japan). At the April 2026 AGM he highlighted the company's AI push.
deep_cut_fact: Before running a distributor he advised them: at BCG (2002-2008) he was on the firm's Industrial Goods leadership team. He holds a Stanford bachelor's degree and a Kellogg MBA.
notes: Goes by 'D.G.'. IR head is Kyle Bland (VP Investor Relations). Data aggregators (MarketScreener) say he was earlier an operations manager at Rain Bird Sprinkler Manufacturing, but no primary source was found, so verify before using it. Grainger sells MRO supplies to data-center builders and utilities, which is a possible podcast angle.

name: Jyoti Agarwal
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder, AU Small Finance Bank; co-founder, Sanjay & Jyoti Agarwal Foundation
profile: Wife of AU Small Finance Bank founder and MD/CEO Sanjay Agarwal. She holds about 3.2% of the Jaipur-based bank (roughly 3.8% in FY21) as part of the promoter group. She was an early director of the group (appointed 2003, since ceased). Her Hurun wealth comes from that stake. AU is moving toward universal bank status.
interesting_fact: AU grew from a Jaipur vehicle-finance NBFC into one of India's first small finance banks and has been asked by the RBI to move the promoter family's ~22% stake into a non-operative holding company before final approval as a universal bank.
deep_cut_fact: She co-founded the Sanjay and Jyoti Agarwal Foundation, which works on education for underprivileged children, road safety and digital empowerment.
notes: Private individual with almost no public profile of her own. Shareholding source: AU Bank MGT-9 FY2020-21 (https://www.au.bank.in/pdfs/other-reports/mgt-7---mgt-9/MGT-9-2020-21.pdf). Best route is via AU Bank corporate communications or the family foundation.

name: Rakesh Kumar
current_role: Founder and Executive Director, Gawar Construction Ltd (Hisar, Haryana)
profile: Co-founder, with his brother Ravinder Kumar, of Gawar Construction, a Hisar-based highway and infrastructure EPC/HAM contractor. It began as a partnership in 1997 and became a limited company in 2008. He sits on the boards of more than 20 Gawar project SPVs for NHAI-style highway concessions across Haryana, Rajasthan, Himachal, Bihar and UP.
interesting_fact: Gawar Construction says it has delivered more than 12,000 lane-kilometres of Indian roads, including expressways, highways, tunnels and bridges for government agencies.
notes: Very common name. The match to Gawar's Rakesh Kumar (DIN 02082036, director since 2008) rests on registry aggregators (tofler, qorpiq) and Dealroom (https://app.dealroom.co/companies/gawar_construction), so it is not fully confirmed. Very low public profile. gawar.in blocks automated access. Best route: the company head office in Hisar.

name: Martin Lawrence
current_role: Actor and stand-up comedian; touring 'Y'all Still Know What It Is!' (2026)
profile: American comedian and actor (born 1965). He co-created and starred in Fox's 'Martin' (1992-97) and plays Marcus Burnett in the four 'Bad Boys' films with Will Smith, the latest being 2024's 'Ride or Die'. Other hits include 'Big Momma's House'. He is back on the road with a national stand-up tour through 2026 and starred in Tubi's sci-fi comedy series 'Demascus' (2025).
interesting_fact: He received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on April 20, 2023, and his 'Bad Boys' role spans nearly three decades, from 1995 to 2024.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Frankfurt, West Germany, while his father served in the US Air Force, and was named after Martin Luther King Jr. and John F. Kennedy. As a teen in Maryland he was a Mid-Atlantic Golden Gloves boxing contender.
notes: Entertainer rather than a business founder, so a weaker fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast. Reach him through his talent agency or publicist; none was verified here. martinlawrence.com is an unrelated art gallery (Martin Lawrence Galleries), so do not use it. He owns a farm near Purcellville, VA. His net worth (~$110M) comes from Wikidata/press estimates.

name: Robert H Dallas Ii
current_role: President, The Dallas Group of America, Inc. (Whitehouse, NJ); Director (founding, since 1991) and 10% owner, Unity Bancorp (UNTY)
profile: Runs The Dallas Group of America, a Whitehouse, NJ specialty-chemical maker of synthetic magnesium silicate adsorbents (Magnesol) used to filter frying oils and purify biodiesel, with plants in the US, the Netherlands and China. He has been a founding director of New Jersey community bank Unity Bancorp since 1991, where his brother David D. Dallas is chairman.
interesting_fact: His company's Magnesol adsorbent helped popularise 'dry wash' biodiesel purification. The company coined the term and launched its D-SOL products in 2002, letting producers skip the water-wash step.
deep_cut_fact: The Dallas Group's original manufacturing plant in Jeffersonville, Indiana marked its 50th anniversary in February 2025.
notes: Age 79 per the 2025 Unity proxy (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/920427/000092042726000020/unty-20251231xdef14a.htm). Low public profile. The biodiesel and renewable-fuel angle suits the energy podcast. Best route: via The Dallas Group of America corporate office or Unity Bancorp's corporate secretary.

name: Beurden Saul Van
current_role: Senior EVP and Head of Artificial Intelligence, Wells Fargo & Company; Operating Committee member
profile: Saul Van Beurden is a Dutch-born banking technologist. He joined Wells Fargo in 2019 from JPMorgan Chase, where he was CIO of Consumer & Community Banking, to become Head of Technology. He then ran Consumer, Small & Business Banking and was co-CEO of Consumer Banking and Lending. He now leads the bank's AI agenda from New York. Earlier he held technology and operations roles at Marsh & McLennan, ING and other Dutch firms.
interesting_fact: As CEO of consumer and small-business banking he oversaw rapid adoption of Wells Fargo's mobile app and modernisation of its national branch network. He is now one of the few big-bank executives whose sole title is Head of AI.
deep_cut_fact: In 2020 he started Wells Fargo's Neurodiversity Hiring program in Technology, which has since spread to other parts of the bank. He is also executive co-sponsor of its Disability Connection employee network.
notes: Name in SEC data is inverted ('Beurden Saul Van'). His AI and data-center-demand angle fits the podcast. Approach through Wells Fargo corporate communications or newsroom. No personal social accounts were verified.

name: Keh Shew Lu
current_role: Director, Diodes Inc (DIOD); retired as Chairman in May 2026 (CEO 2005-2025, Chairman 2020-2026)
profile: Taiwan-born engineer (Tainan; NCKU BSEE 1969; Texas Tech MS/PhD) who rose from junior engineer at Texas Instruments in 1974 to Senior VP running its IC and mixed-signal businesses. He joined the Diodes board in 2001 and as CEO from 2005 built the Plano, TX discrete and analog chipmaker into a multi-billion-dollar company. He handed the CEO role to Gary Yu in 2025 and retired as Chairman in May 2026.
interesting_fact: He was only the second Asian executive, after TSMC founder Morris Chang, to reach Senior Vice President at a major American firm, which he did at Texas Instruments.
deep_cut_fact: As an NCKU undergraduate he published two research papers in IEEE journals. He still funds NCKU scholarships and likes to hire NCKU grads, and NCKU gave him an honorary doctorate in 2021. On receiving it he said, 'Small steps are taken to achieve big goals.'
notes: Uncertain whether he remains a director after the May 2026 annual meeting, so treat the director role as unconfirmed. He founded the DFW Asian-American Citizens Council. Retirement is recent, which makes a reflective 'TI to Diodes' career episode plausible. Power semiconductors connect to data-center and energy topics.

name: M Farooq Kathwari
current_role: Former Chairman, President & CEO, Ethan Allen Interiors (led the company 1988-Nov 2026)
profile: Kashmir-born (1944) Kashmiri-American who emigrated in 1965, worked on Wall Street and earned an NYU MBA. He led furniture maker Ethan Allen as President from 1985 and Chairman/CEO from 1988, making him one of the longest-serving CEOs in US business, and modernised it into a vertically integrated design brand. After a Nov 2026 proxy contest a new board took control, and the company said on 10 Nov 2026 that he 'is no longer with the Company'.
interesting_fact: Carnegie Corporation named him one of its 'Great Immigrants' in 2007. He also served on President Obama's Advisory Commission on Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders.
deep_cut_fact: He came into Ethan Allen as an outsider: he launched a company that supplied Ethan Allen, and Ethan Allen later bought it and eventually made him chairman. His family's Irfan Kathwari Foundation has funded college scholarships for children of Ethan Allen associates for more than two decades.
notes: Major recent change: Doug Bergeron's DGB slate won board control at the 4 Nov 2026 annual meeting. Stefanie Tsen Ward became interim CEO and Bergeron became Executive Chairman, and the release says Kathwari 'is no longer with the Company' (https://ir.ethanallen.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/335/a-new-day-at-ethan-allen). Ethan Allen IR is no longer an appropriate route to him. Treat the topic sensitively. He is active in conflict-resolution and policy circles (Georgetown ISD, Stimson), which may be possible routes. The carnegie.org page supports both the Great Immigrants honour and the supplier-company detail.

name: Brandon Sim
current_role: CEO and President, Astrana Health, Inc. (Nasdaq: ASTH)
profile: Harvard-trained (AB Statistics & Physics, MS CS&E) technologist, age 32 per the 2026 proxy. He was a Citadel Securities quant researcher (2015-19) before joining Astrana (formerly ApolloMed), the LA-based value-based care and physician-network company co-founded by his father Dr. Kenneth Sim. He rose from VP Engineering/CTO/COO to co-CEO in 2021 and sole CEO in 2024, and is leading its tech-driven expansion.
interesting_fact: He went from building trading models at Citadel Securities to running a multi-billion-dollar healthcare company at around 30, overseeing Astrana's 'strategy, growth, operations and technology innovation'.
deep_cut_fact: As a Harvard undergraduate (2012-15) he co-founded and was CTO of Theratech, a medical-device startup developing a low-cost, easy-to-use patch for automated drug delivery.
notes: His father, Dr. Kenneth Sim, is Executive Chairman. Young, technical CEO, which is a plausible guest for AI-in-healthcare and entrepreneurship themes. Personal social accounts were not verified because the search budget was exhausted.

name: Vincent Retort
current_role: Retired (Oct 2, 2026); formerly EVP, Global Reliability & Quality, Lumentum Holdings (LITE)
profile: Optical-components veteran (age 72) who helped run Lumentum, the laser and photonics maker whose transceivers and lasers feed AI data centres, from its 2015 spin-off from JDSU. He was COO 2016-2023, then held roles as chief business officer, president of cloud and networking product development, and head of modules R&D, before retiring in October 2026. Earlier he held engineering roles at JDSU, NeoPhotonics, Seagate and Lightwave Microsystems.
interesting_fact: Over a decade at Lumentum he ran R&D, operations, the Transmission business and the 3D Sensing business unit. His last product roles covered the cloud and networking optics now central to AI data-centre build-outs.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a photonics executive, his degrees are in biology: a BA in Biology from West Virginia University and an MS in Biological Sciences from Stanford.
notes: Newly retired, so Lumentum is no longer a direct route. Strong fit for a data-center/AI-optics episode, since he can speak to the JDSU-to-Lumentum and AI transceiver story. No personal contact channels were verified because the search budget was exhausted. A LinkedIn search by the journalist may help.

name: James M Wehmann
current_role: Retired (Sept 5, 2025); formerly President, Scores, Fair Isaac Corporation (FICO)
profile: Career marketer turned credit-scoring executive. He spent 1993-2000 at catalog retailer Fingerhut, then held marketing roles at Bank One, Brylane and e-commerce firm Digital River. He joined FICO in 2012 as EVP, Scores, and ran its FICO Score business through a period of strong pricing power and share-price gains. He retired in September 2025 to spend time with family and pursue personal interests.
interesting_fact: He ran the FICO Score business, the credit score used in the vast majority of US lending decisions, for more than 13 years. On his retirement CEO Will Lansing said 'Jim leaves an incredibly talented team and a Scores business that is on solid footing.'
deep_cut_fact: Before credit scores, he was a direct-marketing specialist. He spent seven years at Minnesota catalog retailer Fingerhut (1993-2000), rising to SVP Marketing, and later led global marketing at e-commerce platform Digital River (2003-2012).
notes: Retired from FICO in 2025, so the company is not a route to him. Age about 60. Low public profile. A LinkedIn search by the journalist is the likely route. Weak fit for an energy/data-center theme.

name: Jason Raleigh Nunn
current_role: Partner, SR One Capital Management; Director, Zenas BioPharma (ZBIO) and Addex Therapeutics
profile: Jason Nunn is a life-sciences venture investor. He was a partner at New Enterprise Associates (2006-2019) and at MPM Capital's BioEquities Fund (2001-2006) before joining SR One in 2022, where he became a partner in 2024. He has served on many biotech boards, including Dermira (sold to Eli Lilly in 2020), Regulus (sold to Novartis in 2025), Trevena and Hyperion, and he joined Zenas BioPharma's board in May 2024.
interesting_fact: Two of the biotech boards he sat on ended in big-pharma acquisitions: Dermira was bought by Eli Lilly in 2020, and Regulus Therapeutics was bought by Novartis in June 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He started on the public-markets side, as an investment banker at Alex. Brown & Sons and then a healthcare research analyst and portfolio manager at Franklin Templeton. He is a CFA charterholder and member of the CFA Society of San Francisco, with a Dartmouth economics AB and a Stanford MBA.
notes: VC investor rather than a founder. His wealth estimate likely reflects fund-related ZBIO holdings attributed to him in SEC filings. Best route: via SR One. The SR One URL is inferred from the firm name, not found in the filing, so verify it. Biotech focus; weak fit for energy topics.

name: John V Winfield
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, The InterGroup Corporation (INTG); Chairman & CEO, Portsmouth Square Inc.
profile: Los Angeles real-estate investor (age 79 per the 2026 proxy) who has led InterGroup since 1987 and been a director since 1982. Through its subsidiary Portsmouth, InterGroup owns the 558-room Hilton San Francisco Financial District, alongside apartment and commercial properties concentrated in Texas and Southern California, land on Maui, and a securities portfolio.
interesting_fact: His company owns and operates the Hilton San Francisco Financial District at 750 Kearny St. In 2025 it added 14 rooms by converting former administrative offices into guestrooms, taking the hotel to 558 rooms.
deep_cut_fact: He has been CEO of InterGroup for nearly four decades (since 1987), one of the longest tenures of any US public-company CEO. InterGroup still manages its residential rental properties entirely in-house.
notes: Small-cap controlled company. Corporate office at 1516 S. Bundy Dr., Los Angeles (published corporate address, (310) 889-2500). Low media profile. Best route: via the InterGroup corporate office.
